title: Military Madness
subtitle: A lunar war measured in turns
summary: Military Madness is Hudson's turn-based strategy game, first released in Japan as Nectaris on 9 February 1989.
body: Military Madness is Hudson's turn-based strategy game, first released in Japan as Nectaris on 9 February 1989. A war on the Moon in 2089 places the Allied-Union against the Axis-Xenon Empire, whose missile threatens Earth. The player commands a fixed force across hexagonal maps, aiming to occupy an enemy prison camp or eliminate opposing units. Each battlefield is a compact military problem: where to move, which enemy to engage and how to protect the units needed for the next stage of the advance.

Terrain affects ground movement and the outcome of combat, while nearby friendly units strengthen one another. A strong position therefore depends on the shape of the formation as well as the type of vehicle involved. Units gain experience through fighting, giving survival value beyond the immediate encounter. Capturing factories brings access to stored equipment and repairs, so controlling a useful site can change the balance of the map. The player has to coordinate these advantages before an exposed vehicle becomes the opponent's easiest target.

Sixteen basic maps lead to a harder set, with passwords allowing the campaign to continue between sessions. A tutorial explains the rules, and a two-player mode lets another person command the opposition. Jun Chikuma composed the music. The game later reached numerous platforms and was cited as an influence on Dune II. Its original PC Engine release demonstrates how a clear map, a limited set of units and carefully connected combat bonuses can produce a substantial strategy game within a compact console presentation.
